subject.title: [Feature]: WebUI notification system, cron job management popups, and context monitor integration

question: Should OpenClaw add a core connected-Control-UI in-app notification/action queue for cron results and context pressure, and which related action surfaces should share that contract?
rationale: Current main has partial cron, Web Push, and context-monitoring surfaces, but the missing behavior changes Control UI product architecture and overlaps open notification/action issues rather than being a narrow repair.

options.title: Scope Core Notification Queue First
options.body: Define one connected-Control-UI notification/action contract, then wire cron-finished and context-pressure events into it in focused follow-up work.

options.title: Fold Into Related Action Issues
options.body: Make the shared notification/action API work canonical in a related tracker and keep this issue as UX requirements for that broader contract.

options.title: Defer In-App Toasts
options.body: Keep the current inline cron, Web Push, and context-ring surfaces if maintainers decide a core toast/snooze layer is not worth the product complexity.

recommendation.title: Scope Core Notification Queue First
recommendation.body: Define one connected-Control-UI notification/action contract, then wire cron-finished and context-pressure events into it in focused follow-up work.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has prior review context on this issue and the strongest history signal across cron notification routing and related product boundaries.
